Source format: organizational overview

The founding year, 1968, marks the beginning of the Archive's continuous and current operations. It is from this date that the institution's charter, collection policies, and professional practices have evolved, and it remains the official year of establishment recorded in the SSGA charter. The Archive's early years were characterised by grassroots efforts to solicit donations of family papers and to microfilm vulnerable records held by churches, temples, and municipal offices. By the mid-1970s, the collection had grown sufficiently to warrant a dedicated reading room and a small professional staff.

In the decades since, the Archive has expanded its physical premises, digitised significant portions of its holdings, and developed a robust suite of research services. The founding principles of accessibility, preservation, and scholarly integrity continue to guide all strategic decisions.

---

3. COLLECTIONS AND HOLDINGS

The Archive's collections are organised into several principal series, each with its own finding aids and access protocols. The following is a summary of the major holdings areas:

| Series Code | Collection Name | Coverage Period | Physical Format | Access Status |
|-------------|-----------------|-----------------|-----------------|---------------|
| BMD | Civil Registration Registers | 1867–1941 | Bound volumes, microfilm | Open (by appointment) |
| CEN | Census and Population Returns | 1871–1931 | Microfilm, digital scans | Open |
| LND | Land and Property Records | 1830s–1950s | Registers, maps, deeds | Restricted (some items) |
| PRO | Probate and Estate Files | 1840s–1960s | Case files, wills | Open (with redactions) |
| SCH | School and Institutional Records | 1870s–1970s | Registers, admission logs | Open |
| CHR | Ecclesiastical and Temple Records | 1820s–present | Baptism, marriage, burial registers | Varies by congregation |
| FAM | Private Family Papers | 1800s–2000s | Correspondence, diaries, photographs | Donor-restricted |
| ORT | Oral History Interviews | 1980s–present | Audio recordings, transcripts | Open (with consent forms) |

The BMD series, comprising civil registration registers from the Straits Settlements, is the most heavily consulted collection. These registers provide the backbone for many family history research projects and are frequently cross-referenced with church records and census returns. The FAM series, while smaller in volume, offers unique insights into personal lives and social networks, and is a priority for ongoing digitisation.

4. RESEARCH SERVICES AND PUBLIC ACCESS

SSGA offers a tiered service model to accommodate different research needs and levels of expertise.

4.1 On-Site Research
The Reading Room at our main premises is open to all registered patrons. Researchers may access open collections, consult microfilm readers, and request materials from closed stacks. Staff are available during opening hours for guidance on using finding aids and navigating the collections. On-site research is free for members; non-members are charged a daily access fee.

4.2 Remote Research Services
For patrons unable to visit in person, SSGA operates a remote research service. Requests are handled on a first-come, first-served basis, and turnaround times vary depending on the complexity of the enquiry and the availability of digitised materials. A fee schedule applies, with different rates for basic lookups, document retrieval, and extended research projects.

4.3 Digitisation and Reproduction
Photocopying, photography, and digitisation services are available for most open collections, subject to the physical condition of the original material and any donor-imposed restrictions. Reproduction requests are assessed individually, and some items may be excluded from copying due to preservation concerns. Digital surrogates are provided at a standard resolution; higher-resolution scans may be commissioned for research or publication purposes.
The phrase was selected following a consultative process involving staff, trustees, and members of the genealogical research community. It was chosen over several alternatives—among them "Guardians of Heritage", "Linking Lives Across Time", and "Every Family Has a Story"—for its clarity and its emphasis on the active, connective role the Archive plays, rather than a purely custodial one.

The motto is used in both English and, where appropriate, in Malay translation: **"Memelihara Akar, Menghubungkan Generasi"**. This bilingual usage reflects the multilingual character of the collections and the communities they document.

### 6.1 Overview

This section provides guidance for staff, contractors, and partners who produce materials on behalf of SSGA. It is maintained by the Corporate Communications Office and is reviewed annually. The current version was approved on 2024-03-15 and supersedes the previous edition of 2022-11-30.

### 6.2 Logo and Visual Identity

The SSGA logo comprises a stylised banyan tree, rendered in deep green and gold, with roots that extend into the shape of an open book. The tree symbolises continuity, shelter, and the interconnections of family lines; the book represents the documentary record. The logo should always be reproduced from approved digital masters and should not be recoloured, rotated, or placed on busy backgrounds.

Minimum clear space equivalent to the height of the tree canopy must be maintained on all sides. The preferred placement is the top-left corner of printed materials and the top-centre of digital communications.

Primary typeface for print: Source Serif Pro, used for headings and body text. Secondary typeface for digital applications: Source Sans Pro, used for navigation, captions, and interface elements. Fallback typefaces are specified in the digital style sheet maintained by the Web Services Unit.

### 6.4 Use of the Motto in Communications

The institutional motto, "Preserving Roots, Connecting Generations", should be used consistently across all platforms. Guidelines for placement and formatting are as follows:

- **Website homepage:** The motto appears in the header banner, directly beneath the SSGA name and logo.
- **Letterhead:** The motto is printed at the foot of the page, in Archive Green, set in Source Serif Pro italic.
- **Email signatures:** The motto follows the staff member's name and designation, in a single line, without punctuation.
- **Exhibition panels:** The motto may be used as a thematic epigraph on introductory panels; it should not be repeated verbatim on every panel within an exhibition.
- **Publications:** The motto appears on the title page verso of SSGA-published works, alongside the copyright notice.

The motto should not be paraphrased, abbreviated, or combined with other taglines. When translated, the approved Malay rendering "Memelihara Akar, Menghubungkan Generasi" should be used. Translations into Chinese and Tamil are prepared on a case-by-case basis by the Communications Office in consultation with the respective community liaison officers.

### 6.5 Institutional Voice and Tone

All public-facing communications should reflect the following principles:

- **Accessible:** Avoid unnecessary jargon; explain technical or archival terms when first used.
- **Welcoming:** Address readers as potential researchers, not as passive recipients of information.
- **Precise:** Ensure that dates, place names, and record citations are accurate and verifiable.
- **Respectful:** Acknowledge the sensitivity of certain records, particularly those relating to adoption, illegitimacy, or family disputes, and handle such materials with discretion.

## 5. Future Directions and Partnerships

### 5.1 Strategic Goals (2025–2030)

The Straits Settlements Genealogical Archive (SSGA) enters its next planning cycle with a mandate to broaden access to its collections while strengthening the institutional frameworks that ensure their long-term preservation. The Board of Trustees approved the current Strategic Plan at its meeting on 2025-03-14, and the plan identifies four principal goals:

1. **Deepen digital access.** The Archive will continue to expand its online catalogue and digitisation pipeline, with particular attention to records that are currently accessible only on-site. Priority will be given to the Straits Settlements civil registration registers, church records, and the papers of mercantile houses operating in Singapore, Penang, and Malacca before 1942.

2. **Strengthen preservation capacity.** SSGA will invest in the physical infrastructure of its repository, including climate-controlled storage for vulnerable materials and the progressive migration of at-risk audiovisual and photographic formats.

3. **Extend community engagement.** The Archive will develop new programmes for family historians, educational institutions, and diaspora communities with ancestral ties to the Straits Settlements. These programmes will complement the existing Family History Month activities coordinated by the Outreach and Education unit.

4. **Enhance institutional partnerships.** SSGA will formalise and extend its collaborations with national, regional, and international institutions to support research, capacity building, and the exchange of expertise.

The Strategic Plan is supported by an annual work plan, which is reviewed by the Management Committee each January. Progress against the plan's objectives is reported to the Board of Trustees at its quarterly meetings.

### 5.2 Digital Preservation and Systems Development

The Digital Heritage Services Unit, under the leadership of Ms. Lee, will oversee a programme of work over the coming years that includes the following components:

- **Catalogue system renewal.** The Archive will replace its current online catalogue platform with a system that offers improved search functionality, better support for multilingual metadata, and a more accessible interface. The procurement process is expected to begin in the third quarter of 2026, with migration of existing records scheduled to follow in 2027. The current catalogue will remain fully operational throughout the transition.

- **Digitisation of the Straits Settlements Land Records.** A multi-year project is planned to digitise the land registers and associated maps held by the Archive. These records document property ownership, transfers, and disputes across the Straits Settlements and are heavily used by researchers tracing family histories or property lineages. The project will proceed in phases, beginning with the Singapore registers.

- **Format migration for audiovisual materials.** The Archive holds a significant collection of oral history interviews, film reels, and audio recordings dating from the mid-twentieth century. A preservation programme will progressively migrate these materials to digital formats that meet current archival standards, ensuring their continued accessibility as playback equipment becomes obsolete.

- **Bit-level storage integrity.** The Archive will maintain its commitment to bit-level storage integrity for all digital assets, with regular checksum verification and redundant storage across geographically separate locations. This work is carried out in accordance with the digital preservation policy adopted by the Board in 2023.

Ms. Lee's unit will also continue to develop the Archive's public website and social media presence, with a planned redesign of the website to improve navigation and to highlight newly available digital collections.

### 5.3 Partnerships and Collaboration

SSGA maintains a range of partnerships with institutions in Singapore and abroad. These collaborations take a variety of forms, including joint digitisation projects, staff exchanges, shared cataloguing standards, and the organisation of conferences and workshops.

The Archive Portal is the primary public-facing web application for accessing digitized records held by the Digital Heritage Services Division. It provides search, browse, and retrieval functions for archival materials, including photographs, maps, government records, and personal papers.

### 2.2 Service Objectives

- Provide authenticated and unauthenticated access to digitized archival records.
- Support full-text search across OCR-generated text and metadata.
- Deliver high-resolution images with zoom and pan functionality.
- Maintain audit trails for record downloads and user actions.
- Integrate with the Digitized Records Database (DRDB) for content storage and retrieval.

### 2.3 Service Level Expectations

The Portal is expected to achieve:

- 99.5% monthly availability (excluding scheduled maintenance windows).

The Portal follows a three-tier architecture:

### 4. Operational Parameters

This section defines the runtime parameters for the Archive Portal. Values are current as of the version indicated in each subsection. Changes to these parameters are tracked in the deployment notes in Section 6.

#### 4.1 Application Connection Pool

The portal uses HikariCP for PostgreSQL connection pooling. The pool is configured per application node via environment variables or the `application.properties` file.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `pool.maximumPoolSize` | 20 | Maximum number of connections in the pool. |
| `pool.minimumIdle` | 5 | Minimum number of idle connections maintained. |
| `pool.connectionTimeout` | 30000 | Maximum time (ms) to wait for a connection from the pool. |
| `pool.idleTimeout` | 600000 | Maximum time (ms) an idle connection is retained. |
| `pool.maxLifetime` | 1800000 | Maximum lifetime (ms) of a connection in the pool. |
| `pool.validationTimeout` | 5000 | Timeout (ms) for connection validation queries. |

**Guidelines:**

- `maximumPoolSize` should not exceed the `max_connections` setting of the PostgreSQL instance divided by the number of application nodes. For a 3-node deployment, a pool size of 20 per node is safe with a database `max_connections` of 100.
- If connection pool exhaustion is observed, check for long-running queries or unclosed transactions before increasing `maximumPoolSize`. The default `connectionTimeout` of 30 seconds is deliberately short to fail fast under load.
- `minimumIdle` should be set to `0` in auto-scaling environments to avoid holding idle connections during low traffic.

Example configuration block for a production node:

```properties
spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=20
spring.datasource.hikari.minimum-idle=5
spring.datasource.hikari.connection-timeout=30000
spring.datasource.hikari.idle-timeout=600000
spring.datasource.hikari.max-lifetime=1800000
spring.datasource.hikari.validation-timeout=5000
```

#### 4.2 Authentication Service Integration

The portal authenticates users against the National Digital Identity service (Singpass) for public users and against the internal LDAP directory for staff. Integration is handled by the `auth` microservice.

**Singpass Integration:**

| `auth.singpass.issuer` | `https://sts.singpass.gov.sg` | Issuer URL for JWT validation. |
| `auth.singpass.audience` | `archive-portal-prod` | Expected audience claim. |
| `auth.singpass.jwks-url` | `https://sts.singpass.gov.sg/.well-known/jwks.json` | JWKS endpoint for public key retrieval. |
| `auth.singpass.clock-skew` | `30` | Allowed clock skew in seconds. |
| `auth.singpass.session-timeout` | `1800` | Idle session timeout in seconds. |

**LDAP Integration (Staff):**

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| `auth.ldap.url` | `ldap://ldap.internal.sg:389` | Internal LDAP endpoint. |
| `auth.ldap.base-dn` | `ou=people,dc=archives,dc=gov,dc=sg` | Base DN for user lookups. |
| `auth.ldap.user-filter` | `(uid={0})` | Search filter for username. |
| `auth.ldap.group-filter` | `memberOf=cn=portal-staff,ou=groups,dc=archives,dc=gov,dc=sg` | Only users in this group can access staff features. |
| `auth.ldap.connect-timeout` | `5000` | Timeout in ms for initial connection. |
| `auth.ldap.read-timeout` | `10000` | Timeout in ms for read operations. |

**Token Validation:**

- The portal validates the JWT signature on every request. The public keys are cached from the JWKS endpoint for 10 minutes (`auth.singpass.jwks-cache-ttl`).
- If the JWKS endpoint is unreachable, the portal will serve cached keys for up to 1 hour. After that, authentication requests will fail with a `503 Service Unavailable` error until connectivity is restored. The `/health` endpoint reports the status of the key cache.
- Staff sessions are established via a server-side session cookie after successful LDAP bind. The session is stored in Redis with a TTL of 8 hours.

The founding year, 1968, marks the beginning of the Archive's continuous and current operations. It is from this date that the institution's charter, collection policies, and professional practices have evolved, and it remains the official year of establishment recorded in the SSGA charter. The Archive's early years were characterised by grassroots efforts to solicit donations of family papers and to microfilm vulnerable records held by churches, temples, and municipal offices. By the mid-1970s, the collection had grown sufficiently to warrant a dedicated reading room and a small professional staff.

In the decades since, the Archive has expanded its physical premises, digitised significant portions of its holdings, and developed a robust suite of research services. The founding principles of accessibility, preservation, and scholarly integrity continue to guide all strategic decisions.

---

3. COLLECTIONS AND HOLDINGS

The Archive's collections are organised into several principal series, each with its own finding aids and access protocols. The following is a summary of the major holdings areas:

| Series Code | Collection Name | Coverage Period | Physical Format | Access Status |
|-------------|-----------------|-----------------|-----------------|---------------|
| BMD | Civil Registration Registers | 1867–1941 | Bound volumes, microfilm | Open (by appointment) |
| CEN | Census and Population Returns | 1871–1931 | Microfilm, digital scans | Open |
| LND | Land and Property Records | 1830s–1950s | Registers, maps, deeds | Restricted (some items) |
| PRO | Probate and Estate Files | 1840s–1960s | Case files, wills | Open (with redactions) |
| SCH | School and Institutional Records | 1870s–1970s | Registers, admission logs | Open |
| CHR | Ecclesiastical and Temple Records | 1820s–present | Baptism, marriage, burial registers | Varies by congregation |
| FAM | Private Family Papers | 1800s–2000s | Correspondence, diaries, photographs | Donor-restricted |
| ORT | Oral History Interviews | 1980s–present | Audio recordings, transcripts | Open (with consent forms) |

The BMD series, comprising civil registration registers from the Straits Settlements, is the most heavily consulted collection. These registers provide the backbone for many family history research projects and are frequently cross-referenced with church records and census returns. The FAM series, while smaller in volume, offers unique insights into personal lives and social networks, and is a priority for ongoing digitisation.

Straits Settlements Genealogical Archive founded year 1968 year. Record status: current.

---

4. RESEARCH SERVICES AND PUBLIC ACCESS

SSGA offers a tiered service model to accommodate different research needs and levels of expertise.

4.1 On-Site Research
The Reading Room at our main premises is open to all registered patrons. Researchers may access open collections, consult microfilm readers, and request materials from closed stacks. Staff are available during opening hours for guidance on using finding aids and navigating the collections. On-site research is free for members; non-members are charged a daily access fee.

4.2 Remote Research Services
For patrons unable to visit in person, SSGA operates a remote research service. Requests are handled on a first-come, first-served basis, and turnaround times vary depending on the complexity of the enquiry and the availability of digitised materials. A fee schedule applies, with different rates for basic lookups, document retrieval, and extended research projects.

4.3 Digitisation and Reproduction
Photocopying, photography, and digitisation services are available for most open collections, subject to the physical condition of the original material and any donor-imposed restrictions. Reproduction requests are assessed individually, and some items may be excluded from copying due to preservation concerns. Digital surrogates are provided at a standard resolution; higher-resolution scans may be commissioned for research or publication purposes.

The phrase was selected following a consultative process involving staff, trustees, and members of the genealogical research community. It was chosen over several alternatives—among them "Guardians of Heritage", "Linking Lives Across Time", and "Every Family Has a Story"—for its clarity and its emphasis on the active, connective role the Archive plays, rather than a purely custodial one.

The motto is used in both English and, where appropriate, in Malay translation: **"Memelihara Akar, Menghubungkan Generasi"**. This bilingual usage reflects the multilingual character of the collections and the communities they document.

---

## 6. BRANDING GUIDELINES AND PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS

### 6.1 Overview

This section provides guidance for staff, contractors, and partners who produce materials on behalf of SSGA. It is maintained by the Corporate Communications Office and is reviewed annually. The current version was approved on 2024-03-15 and supersedes the previous edition of 2022-11-30.

### 6.2 Logo and Visual Identity

The SSGA logo comprises a stylised banyan tree, rendered in deep green and gold, with roots that extend into the shape of an open book. The tree symbolises continuity, shelter, and the interconnections of family lines; the book represents the documentary record. The logo should always be reproduced from approved digital masters and should not be recoloured, rotated, or placed on busy backgrounds.

Minimum clear space equivalent to the height of the tree canopy must be maintained on all sides. The preferred placement is the top-left corner of printed materials and the top-centre of digital communications.

**Approved colour palette:**

The organizational overview states that the institutional motto of the Straits Settlements Genealogical Archive is 'Preserving Roots, Connecting Generations'. Record status: current.

| Colour | Pantone | CMYK | RGB |
|--------|---------|------|-----|
| Archive Green | PMS 3425 C | C80 M30 Y90 K10 | R0 G105 B60 |
| Heritage Gold | PMS 871 C | C20 M40 Y90 K20 | R150 G120 B60 |
| Neutral Sand | PMS 7527 C | C5 M10 Y25 K10 | R230 G215 B180 |
| Ink Black | PMS Black 6 C | C60 M40 Y40 K100 | R20 G20 B20 |

### 6.3 Typography

Primary typeface for print: Source Serif Pro, used for headings and body text. Secondary typeface for digital applications: Source Sans Pro, used for navigation, captions, and interface elements. Fallback typefaces are specified in the digital style sheet maintained by the Web Services Unit.

### 6.4 Use of the Motto in Communications

The institutional motto, "Preserving Roots, Connecting Generations", should be used consistently across all platforms. Guidelines for placement and formatting are as follows:

- **Website homepage:** The motto appears in the header banner, directly beneath the SSGA name and logo.
- **Letterhead:** The motto is printed at the foot of the page, in Archive Green, set in Source Serif Pro italic.
- **Email signatures:** The motto follows the staff member's name and designation, in a single line, without punctuation.
- **Exhibition panels:** The motto may be used as a thematic epigraph on introductory panels; it should not be repeated verbatim on every panel within an exhibition.
- **Publications:** The motto appears on the title page verso of SSGA-published works, alongside the copyright notice.

The motto should not be paraphrased, abbreviated, or combined with other taglines. When translated, the approved Malay rendering "Memelihara Akar, Menghubungkan Generasi" should be used. Translations into Chinese and Tamil are prepared on a case-by-case basis by the Communications Office in consultation with the respective community liaison officers.

### 6.5 Institutional Voice and Tone

All public-facing communications should reflect the following principles:

- **Accessible:** Avoid unnecessary jargon; explain technical or archival terms when first used.
- **Welcoming:** Address readers as potential researchers, not as passive recipients of information.
- **Precise:** Ensure that dates, place names, and record citations are accurate and verifiable.
- **Respectful:** Acknowledge the sensitivity of certain records, particularly those relating to adoption, illegitimacy, or family disputes, and handle such materials with discretion.

The Straits Settlements Genealogical Archive (SSGA) is administered by a leadership team that combines expertise in archival science, digital technology, and community engagement. The following directory reflects the organisational structure as of the 2025 annual review. All titles and responsibilities are current as of the date of publication.

## 7.1 Leadership Team

### Director of the Archive
**Mr. Tan Kian Huat** assumed the role of Director of the Straits Settlements Genealogical Archive on 2021-04-01, succeeding Dr. Faridah binte Ahmad, who served from 2013 to 2021. Mr. Tan holds a Master of Arts in Archival Studies from the University of British Columbia and previously served as Deputy Director of Records Management at the National Archives of Singapore. He oversees the strategic direction of the Archive, including acquisitions, public programming, and international partnerships. Mr. Tan reports directly to the Board of Governors and serves as the Archive's principal representative to the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth.

### Deputy Director (Collections and Access)
**Dr. Nalini Krishnan** joined the Archive in 2018 as Head of Reference Services and was promoted to Deputy Director (Collections and Access) on 2023-01-01. Dr. Krishnan holds a Doctor of Philosophy in Southeast Asian History from the National University of Singapore and has published extensively on migration patterns in the Straits Settlements. Her portfolio encompasses the acquisitions unit, cataloguing and metadata services, the reading room, and the public reference desk. She chairs the Collections Development Committee, which meets quarterly to review proposed acquisitions and deaccessions.

### Head of Digital Heritage Services
**Ms. Lee Mei Ling** serves as Head of Digital Heritage Services, a position she has held since 2019-06-01. The organizational overview lists Lee Mei Ling's job title as Head of Digital Heritage Services. Record status: current. Ms. Lee holds a Bachelor of Science in Computer Science from Nanyang Technological University and a Graduate Certificate in Digital Curation from the University of Melbourne. She leads the Digital Heritage Services Unit, which is responsible for:

- The SSGA Online Catalogue and its underlying database systems
- Digitisation of physical records, including photographs, maps, and bound volumes
- Digital preservation, including format migration and bit-level storage integrity
- The Archive's public website and social media presence
- Development of digital research tools and finding aids

Ms. Lee previously worked at the National Library Board as a Senior Librarian in the Digital Library Division, where she managed the digitisation of the Singapore-Malaysia Collection. She represents SSGA on the Southeast Asian Digital Heritage Network and has presented on digital preservation strategies at conferences in Kuala Lumpur, Bangkok, and Manila.

### Head of Outreach and Education
**Mdm. Rosnah binte Omar** has served as Head of Outreach and Education since 2017. A former secondary school history teacher with the Ministry of Education, Mdm. Rosnah joined SSGA in 2014 as an Education Officer. Her unit manages the Archive's school programmes, public lectures, exhibition programme, and community engagement initiatives, including the annual Family History Month held each August. She is a member of the Singapore Heritage Society and serves on the advisory committee for the Eurasian Association's heritage programmes.

### Head of Corporate Services
**Mr. Ganesh s/o Rajendran** joined SSGA in 2020 as Head of Corporate Services. Mr. Ganesh holds a Master of Business Administration from Singapore Management University and previously worked in the finance division of a regional logistics company. His portfolio covers human resources, finance and procurement, facilities management, and information technology infrastructure (excluding the digital heritage systems managed by Ms. Lee's unit). He also coordinates the Archive's business continuity planning and risk management activities.

# Straits Settlements Genealogical Archive: Organizational Overview

## 5. Future Directions and Partnerships

### 5.1 Strategic Goals (2025–2030)

The Straits Settlements Genealogical Archive (SSGA) enters its next planning cycle with a mandate to broaden access to its collections while strengthening the institutional frameworks that ensure their long-term preservation. The Board of Trustees approved the current Strategic Plan at its meeting on 2025-03-14, and the plan identifies four principal goals:

1. **Deepen digital access.** The Archive will continue to expand its online catalogue and digitisation pipeline, with particular attention to records that are currently accessible only on-site. Priority will be given to the Straits Settlements civil registration registers, church records, and the papers of mercantile houses operating in Singapore, Penang, and Malacca before 1942.

2. **Strengthen preservation capacity.** SSGA will invest in the physical infrastructure of its repository, including climate-controlled storage for vulnerable materials and the progressive migration of at-risk audiovisual and photographic formats.

3. **Extend community engagement.** The Archive will develop new programmes for family historians, educational institutions, and diaspora communities with ancestral ties to the Straits Settlements. These programmes will complement the existing Family History Month activities coordinated by the Outreach and Education unit.

4. **Enhance institutional partnerships.** SSGA will formalise and extend its collaborations with national, regional, and international institutions to support research, capacity building, and the exchange of expertise.

The Strategic Plan is supported by an annual work plan, which is reviewed by the Management Committee each January. Progress against the plan's objectives is reported to the Board of Trustees at its quarterly meetings.

### 5.2 Digital Preservation and Systems Development

The Digital Heritage Services Unit, under the leadership of Ms. Lee, will oversee a programme of work over the coming years that includes the following components:

- **Catalogue system renewal.** The Archive will replace its current online catalogue platform with a system that offers improved search functionality, better support for multilingual metadata, and a more accessible interface. The procurement process is expected to begin in the third quarter of 2026, with migration of existing records scheduled to follow in 2027. The current catalogue will remain fully operational throughout the transition.

- **Digitisation of the Straits Settlements Land Records.** A multi-year project is planned to digitise the land registers and associated maps held by the Archive. These records document property ownership, transfers, and disputes across the Straits Settlements and are heavily used by researchers tracing family histories or property lineages. The project will proceed in phases, beginning with the Singapore registers.

- **Format migration for audiovisual materials.** The Archive holds a significant collection of oral history interviews, film reels, and audio recordings dating from the mid-twentieth century. A preservation programme will progressively migrate these materials to digital formats that meet current archival standards, ensuring their continued accessibility as playback equipment becomes obsolete.

- **Bit-level storage integrity.** The Archive will maintain its commitment to bit-level storage integrity for all digital assets, with regular checksum verification and redundant storage across geographically separate locations. This work is carried out in accordance with the digital preservation policy adopted by the Board in 2023.

Ms. Lee's unit will also continue to develop the Archive's public website and social media presence, with a planned redesign of the website to improve navigation and to highlight newly available digital collections.

### 5.3 Partnerships and Collaboration

SSGA maintains a range of partnerships with institutions in Singapore and abroad. These collaborations take a variety of forms, including joint digitisation projects, staff exchanges, shared cataloguing standards, and the organisation of conferences and workshops.

The Archive Portal is the primary public-facing web application for accessing digitized records held by the Digital Heritage Services Division. It provides search, browse, and retrieval functions for archival materials, including photographs, maps, government records, and personal papers.

The Portal was launched on 2024-03-18 and is currently in active service. This launch date is recorded in the deployment register (see Section 7.1) and remains the current controlled entry for the service's initial availability.

### 2.2 Service Objectives

- Provide authenticated and unauthenticated access to digitized archival records.
- Support full-text search across OCR-generated text and metadata.
- Deliver high-resolution images with zoom and pan functionality.
- Maintain audit trails for record downloads and user actions.
- Integrate with the Digitized Records Database (DRDB) for content storage and retrieval.

### 2.3 Service Level Expectations

The Portal is expected to achieve:

- 99.5% monthly availability (excluding scheduled maintenance windows).
- Median search response time under 800 ms during normal load.
- Maximum concurrent sessions of 2,500 without degradation.

These expectations are reviewed quarterly by the Digital Heritage Services Division.

---

## 3. Architecture

The system documentation notes that the Archive Portal had its launch date on 2024-03-18. Record status: current.

### 3.1 High-Level Architecture

The Portal follows a three-tier architecture:

1. **Presentation Tier:** Web front-end served via Nginx, with client-side JavaScript for search and viewer functionality.
2. **Application Tier:** Java-based Spring Boot application handling business logic, authentication, and API endpoints.
3. **Data Tier:** PostgreSQL database (DRDB) for metadata and user data, with an S3-compatible object store for digitized images and documents.

All tiers are deployed within the Singapore region, with infrastructure hosted on the government cloud platform.

### 4. Operational Parameters

This section defines the runtime parameters for the Archive Portal. Values are current as of the version indicated in each subsection. Changes to these parameters are tracked in the deployment notes in Section 6.

#### 4.1 Application Connection Pool

The portal uses HikariCP for PostgreSQL connection pooling. The pool is configured per application node via environment variables or the `application.properties` file.

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `pool.maximumPoolSize` | 20 | Maximum number of connections in the pool. |
| `pool.minimumIdle` | 5 | Minimum number of idle connections maintained. |
| `pool.connectionTimeout` | 30000 | Maximum time (ms) to wait for a connection from the pool. |
| `pool.idleTimeout` | 600000 | Maximum time (ms) an idle connection is retained. |
| `pool.maxLifetime` | 1800000 | Maximum lifetime (ms) of a connection in the pool. |
| `pool.validationTimeout` | 5000 | Timeout (ms) for connection validation queries. |

**Guidelines:**

- `maximumPoolSize` should not exceed the `max_connections` setting of the PostgreSQL instance divided by the number of application nodes. For a 3-node deployment, a pool size of 20 per node is safe with a database `max_connections` of 100.
- If connection pool exhaustion is observed, check for long-running queries or unclosed transactions before increasing `maximumPoolSize`. The default `connectionTimeout` of 30 seconds is deliberately short to fail fast under load.
- `minimumIdle` should be set to `0` in auto-scaling environments to avoid holding idle connections during low traffic.

Example configuration block for a production node:

```properties
spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size=20
spring.datasource.hikari.minimum-idle=5
spring.datasource.hikari.connection-timeout=30000
spring.datasource.hikari.idle-timeout=600000
spring.datasource.hikari.max-lifetime=1800000
spring.datasource.hikari.validation-timeout=5000
```

#### 4.2 Authentication Service Integration

The portal authenticates users against the National Digital Identity service (Singpass) for public users and against the internal LDAP directory for staff. Integration is handled by the `auth` microservice.

**Singpass Integration:**

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| `auth.singpass.enabled` | `true` | Master switch for Singpass login. |
| `auth.singpass.issuer` | `https://sts.singpass.gov.sg` | Issuer URL for JWT validation. |
| `auth.singpass.audience` | `archive-portal-prod` | Expected audience claim. |
| `auth.singpass.jwks-url` | `https://sts.singpass.gov.sg/.well-known/jwks.json` | JWKS endpoint for public key retrieval. |
| `auth.singpass.clock-skew` | `30` | Allowed clock skew in seconds. |
| `auth.singpass.session-timeout` | `1800` | Idle session timeout in seconds. |

**LDAP Integration (Staff):**

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| `auth.ldap.url` | `ldap://ldap.internal.sg:389` | Internal LDAP endpoint. |
| `auth.ldap.base-dn` | `ou=people,dc=archives,dc=gov,dc=sg` | Base DN for user lookups. |
| `auth.ldap.user-filter` | `(uid={0})` | Search filter for username. |
| `auth.ldap.group-filter` | `memberOf=cn=portal-staff,ou=groups,dc=archives,dc=gov,dc=sg` | Only users in this group can access staff features. |
| `auth.ldap.connect-timeout` | `5000` | Timeout in ms for initial connection. |
| `auth.ldap.read-timeout` | `10000` | Timeout in ms for read operations. |

**Token Validation:**

- The portal validates the JWT signature on every request. The public keys are cached from the JWKS endpoint for 10 minutes (`auth.singpass.jwks-cache-ttl`).
- If the JWKS endpoint is unreachable, the portal will serve cached keys for up to 1 hour. After that, authentication requests will fail with a `503 Service Unavailable` error until connectivity is restored. The `/health` endpoint reports the status of the key cache.
- Staff sessions are established via a server-side session cookie after successful LDAP bind. The session is stored in Redis with a TTL of 8 hours.
